item.title: A nonstandard fractional Jacobi pseudospectral method for weakly regular right-sided Caputo terminal problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.20829v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Right-sided fractional differential equations arising in terminal value problems present substantial analytical and numerical challenges due to their intrinsic nonlocal structure and the presence of weak algebraic-type singularities near the terminal point. These singular behaviors significantly degrade the performance of classical finite-difference, finite-element, and standard spectral methods, which typically rely on smoothness assumptions that break down in the fractional setting. In this work, we develop a comprehensive fractional pseudospectral framework specifically designed for nonlinear right-sided Caputo terminal value systems. The proposed method employs a versatile family of nonstandard fractional Jacobi basis functions whose endpoint-weighted structure naturally reflects the asymptotic behavior of right-sided fractional operators. This construction enables the accurate approximation of solutions with limited regularity near the terminal point, without requiring smoothing transformations or mesh grading. We establish the existence and uniqueness of the discrete numerical solution and derive rigorous convergence estimates that faithfully capture the inherent singularity structure of the problem. A series of numerical experiments validates the theoretical developments and demonstrates that the proposed approach delivers high-order accuracy and superior resolution of terminal-layer behavior compared with traditional spectral techniques. The resulting framework provides an efficient and reliable computational tool for challenging nonlinear fractional terminal value systems characterized by weak solution regularity.
item.dc:creator: Ibrahem G. Ameen, Magda Hammad, Mohsen Razzaghi, Mahmoud A. Zaky

item.title: A Coupled Fluid Naghdi Shell Windkessel Model for Pulmonary Artery Banding: Partitioned Numerical Scheme and Parameter Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2610.20966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a 3D fluid structure interaction model for blood flow through deformable vessels with localized constrictions, motivated by pulmonary artery banding in neonates with congenital heart disease. The model couples incompressible Navier Stokes equations in an Arbitrary Lagrangian Eulerian framework with a Naghdi shell model for the arterial wall and a three element Windkessel model for downstream circulation. The shell describes a 3D cylindrical vessel wall with variable radius and is defined on a 2D reference domain. Its low regularity formulation retains membrane, bending, and transverse shear deformation while requiring only first derivatives of the reference midsurface, accommodating piecewise smooth geometries with discontinuous surface slopes. We derive the coupled variational formulation and develop a non-iterative partitioned scheme with a Robin-type interface condition incorporating arterial wall inertia. For a linearized fixed domain problem, we establish a discrete energy estimate under suitable assumptions. A unscented Kalman filter estimates proximal and distal resistances and compliance from inlet-pressure observations. Numerical experiments demonstrate consistent pressure wave propagation and wall deformation under spatial and temporal refinement. Comparisons of the standard Naghdi shell and a modified, predominantly radial shell model reveal how structural deformation mechanisms affect wave speed and displacement. An idealized pulmonary artery banding example demonstrates the coupled fluid shell Windkessel model with parameter estimation. The framework enables investigation of the hemodynamic and mechanical effects of localized constrictions and their dependence on downstream vascular properties.
item.dc:creator: Yifan Wang, Josip Tambaca, Suncica Canic

item.title: Galerkin finite element method for time fractional diffusion-wave equations with constant time delay
item.description: arXiv:2610.21056v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies numerical methods for the time fractional diffusion-wave equations with the constant delay. Using a symmetric fractional-order reduction technique and introducing the auxiliary variable $w$, we reformulate the original problem as an equivalent coupled system and for the first time carry out a rigorous regularity analysis of $w$. Based on the symmetric graded time mesh, the coupled problem is discretised by the $L1$ scheme in time and a standard finite element method in space, and the stability result of the developed fully discrete finite element scheme is established by means of a discrete fractional Gr\"onwall inequality. Furthermore, we derive a new comparison principle and reconstruct a new barrier function on each interval $((k-1)\tau,k\tau]$, $1\le k\le K$ according to the properties of the symmetric graded mesh. Based on the new barrier function, we obtain new relevant properties, which lead to a novel and crucial stability property for the discrete fractional operator. Combining the obtained local truncation error in time gives a local error estimate for the fully discrete finite element scheme, which shows that our convergence result provides a unified framework that seamlessly encompasses both pointwise-in-time error estimates on uniform meshes and global-in-time error estimates on symmetrical graded meshes. Numerical experiments confirm the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Xuan Li, Kaile Qiu, Chaobao Huang, Weiping Bu

item.title: Adaptive Randomized Neural Networks for PDEs: Structure-Aware Feature Redistribution and Residual-Driven Block Enrichment
item.description: arXiv:2610.21077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Randomized neural networks retain an output-linear least-squares solve, but globally sampled random features may fail to capture the spatial and scale structure of PDE solutions. We propose SFRBE--RaNN, a two-stage adaptive trial-space construction. SFR redistributes a fixed feature budget according to regional indicator masses and adapts regional weight scales through low-dimensional residual-based optimization. RBE constructs nonredundant enrichments by screening multiple activation families, removing represented response directions, and selecting the smallest admissible prefix. For solution-dependent operators, candidates are screened with a frozen operator and accepted only after nonlinear residual verification. For fixed linear problems, we establish an exact discrete residual-reduction identity and a conditional solution-error estimate. Building on this identity, we combine safeguarded SFR with RBE capture factors to derive a finite-horizon error bound involving baseline best approximation and empirical consistency, together with a conditional random-search success-probability bound. Numerical experiments on localized, multiscale, and nonlinear space--time problems demonstrate the method's effectiveness.
item.dc:creator: You Yang, Fei Wang

item.title: A geometric criterion for the dimension of Morgan-Scott spline spaces $S_{2r}^r(\Delta_{\mathrm{MS}})$
item.description: arXiv:2610.21192v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a geometric dimension criterion for spline spaces on nondegenerate standard Morgan-Scott triangulations with four distinct edge directions at each interior vertex. For every integer $r\ge1$, concurrence of the three auxiliary lines joining corresponding interior and boundary vertices implies that $\dim S_{2r}^r(\Delta_{\mathrm{MS}})$ exceeds the Schumaker lower bound by one. The proof constructs a quadratic form through the six dual spoke points and uses its $r$th power to define a nonzero functional annihilating the image of the smoothing-cofactor map. Diener's upper bound then gives the dimension formula. We also give a matrix representation of this functional and an explicit example in the quadratic case. Combined with the known necessary conditions and the negative-branch exclusion of Deng, Feng, and Kozak, the result yields a necessary and sufficient concurrence criterion for $r>2$.
item.dc:creator: Xinyu Wu, Yi Zheng, Jiansong Deng

item.title: A Hybrid High-Order method for variable-exponent Leray-Lions problems with convergence under minimal regularity
item.description: arXiv:2610.21598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a homogeneous Dirichlet problem for nonlinear elliptic equations in divergence form with Leray--Lions fluxes of variable growth. The class includes the variable-exponent $p(\cdot)$-Laplacian and regularized Carreau--Yasuda-type laws. We propose and analyze a Hybrid High-Order (HHO) discretization on general polytopal meshes, a hybrid nonconforming method based on cell and face polynomial unknowns of arbitrary degree. We develop a variable-exponent polynomial and discrete functional toolkit centered on a mean-exponent norm equivalence, together with inverse, trace, Poincar\'e--Wirtinger, Sobolev--Poincar\'e, discrete Lebesgue embedding, interpolation, and compactness estimates adapted to HHO unknowns. We then establish well-posedness of the nonlinear discrete problem and convergence without assuming additional regularity of the exact solution beyond its natural energy space. The discrete potential converges strongly in every uniformly subcritical variable-exponent Lebesgue space, the reconstructed gradient converges strongly in the natural variable-exponent space, and the stabilization energy vanishes. Numerical experiments in two, three, and four space dimensions confirm convergence for singular solutions and for exponent fields ranging from close to $1$ up to $6$. Quantitative a priori error estimates for the same method are derived in a companion paper.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e Harnist, Romain Mottier

item.title: On the stability of basis construction in extended Krylov subspace methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.21603v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Extended Krylov subspace methods (EKSMs) are a well known approach for approximating the action of a matrix function on a vector $f(A)\mathbf{b}$, and their block versions are often used for solving Lyapunov and Sylvester matrix equations. EKSMs produce Laurent approximations to the underlying operator, which are generally more accurate per iteration than polynomial KSMs, without requiring a pole selection procedure as rational KSMs do. At the same time, due to the expansion of the search space by not only $A$ but also by its inverse, a number of implementation choices must be made that can affect the stability of the algorithm in floating-point arithmetic. We concentrate on two variants that often appear in the literature and in code, based on whether new basis vectors are built via what we denote as ``mixed channels" or ``split channels." We characterize their loss of orthogonality with an easily computable metric and prove that when $A$ is symmetric positive definite, mixed channels have better orthogonality than split channels; however, numerical experiments demonstrate that straightforward predictions are not possible for indefinite or nonsymmetric matrices. We also provide a modular MATLAB toolbox, \texttt{ektoolbox}, that contains new versions of EKSMs with low-synchronization Gram-Schmidt backbones.
item.dc:creator: Kathryn Lund, Marcel Schweitzer

item.title: A priori error estimates for a Hybrid High-Order method on variable-exponent Leray-Lions problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.21611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive a priori error estimates for the Hybrid High-Order (HHO) discretization of variable-exponent Leray--Lions problems introduced in a companion convergence study. HHO methods belong to the family of hybrid nonconforming methods, based on cell and face polynomial unknowns of arbitrary degree. Under additional broken regularity of the exact solution and its flux, we establish a localized error estimate that retains the individual element sizes and a global estimate whose rate distinguishes the purely subquadratic, mixed subquadratic--superquadratic, and purely superquadratic regimes. In the subquadratic range, we also derive a regime-dependent refinement that compares the local approximation scale with the local non-degeneracy scale and recovers the optimal polynomial order when that scale is resolved by the mesh. The analysis relies on variable-exponent approximation properties of polynomial projectors, mean-exponent tools for discrete polynomial spaces, and weighted monotonicity estimates. The framework also covers regularized and mildly non-symmetric anisotropic Carreau--Yasuda-type fluxes. Numerical experiments on Cartesian and Voronoi meshes support the predicted rates and show that the regularity assumption on the flux cannot be dispensed with.
item.dc:creator: Andr\'e Harnist, Romain Mottier

item.title: Greedy multiscale kernel algorithms
item.description: arXiv:2610.21615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multiscale kernel approximation and greedy kernel algorithms are two established tools for scattered data approximation. We combine them into greedy multiscale kernel algorithms, in which every level of a multiscale residual correction is constructed by a greedy kernel algorithm. For the multiscale $f$-greedy algorithm we prove convergence rates in the number of selected centres which coincide (up to an arbitrarily small loss in the exponent) with the rates of the single-scale $f$-greedy algorithm. The gain of the multiscale construction is in the stability, and we make this precise by a two-sided estimate for the condition number of kernel matrices with rescaled kernels. The lower bound shows that any single-scale method, and in particular the $f$-greedy algorithm, pays for its convergence rate with condition numbers growing at least like a power of the number of centres. In contrast, the multiscale scaling of the kernel keeps this lower bound fixed on every level without changing the rate. The upper bound identifies the separation of the centres at the scale of the kernel as the quantity to control. We give the operation counts of all the methods considered and compare the greedy multiscale algorithms numerically with single-scale greedy and classical multiscale methods, in terms of error, time and conditioning.
item.dc:creator: Sara Avesani, Armin Iske, Michael Multerer, Tizian Wenzel

item.title: Projection-Based Parareal for Nonlinear Initial-Value Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.21680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parareal is a parallel-in-time method for initial-value problems that has found extensive applications and given rise to many variants. Krylov-enhanced parareal is a variant of parareal that uses projection techniques to accelerate convergence substantially for linear problems. In this paper, we study a projection-based parareal algorithm for nonlinear initial-value problems with a modified iteration scheme and an arbitrary orthogonal projection. For a general nonlinear problem, we prove a convergence estimate for each iteration step on a fixed time grid. We analyze the errors of the modified scheme and the scheme of Krylov-enhanced parareal relative to the old error as the coarse grid is refined. For a coarse solver of order $p$ and step size $h$, we prove error bounds of $O(h^{p+1})$ for the modified scheme and $O(h)$ for that of Krylov-enhanced parareal at the first potentially inexact time point under mild assumptions. Numerical experiments on two nonlinear problems are consistent with the theoretical analysis.
item.dc:creator: Chenyi Tan, Yuncheng Xu, Yehao Zhang, Yangfeng Su

item.title: The $L\log L$-Luxemburg Discrepancy for Nonnegative Weights Suffers from the Curse of Dimensionality
item.description: arXiv:2610.21717v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the normalized discrepancy in the Luxemburg norm generated by $\Phi(s)=s\log(1+s)$. For arbitrary nonnegative quadrature weights, we prove that the associated information complexity suffers from the curse of dimensionality: for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, there exist constants $c_\varepsilon>0$ and $d_0=d_0(\varepsilon)\in\mathbb{N}$ such that \[N_{\Phi,+}(\varepsilon,d)\ge c_{\varepsilon} d^{-1}(1.07735\ldots)^d \qquad \mbox{for all } d\ge d_0. \] The result therefore also applies to equal-weight quasi-Monte Carlo rules.
item.dc:creator: Josef Dick, Friedrich Pillichshammer

item.title: Stability analysis of the steady solution for incompressible lid-driven cavity flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.21721v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Steady solutions at high Reynolds numbers are computed using an iterative method that linearizes the nonlinear convective terms. This linearization reduces the original nonlinear boundary-value problem to a sequence of linear problems, one solved at each iteration, thereby improving the numerical robustness of the algorithm and enabling convergence over a wide range of governing parameters. The stability of steady incompressible fluid flows is studied within the framework of a linear problem for perturbations. The original steady velocity and pressure fields are subjected to small perturbations, after which the equations are linearized with respect to the perturbations. The resulting linear problem allows one to analyze the evolution of small perturbations and to establish whether the steady solutions under consideration are stable with respect to infinitesimal perturbations. In this work, the computational implementation is based on spatial discretization by the finite element method on triangular meshes. The stability of the obtained solutions is analyzed by solving a generalized algebraic eigenvalue problem formed after discretization of the linear problem for perturbations. The presence of eigenvalues with positive real part indicates instability, whereas their absence indicates stability. Calculations were performed on a sequence of refined meshes at various Reynolds numbers for the flow in a square cavity.
item.dc:creator: Dmitri Lomasov, Petr Vabishchevich

item.title: An IMEX multi-level domain-decomposition method for the Boltzmann equation on unstructured meshes
item.description: arXiv:2610.21740v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a dynamically adaptive multi-level method for the multiscale Boltzmann equation on unstructured meshes, coupling the compressible Euler, Navier-Stokes, and full Boltzmann descriptions within a single asymptotic-preserving IMEX framework. Unlike standard domain-decomposition approaches, where independent solvers exchange data only through interface conditions, the three models form a unified multiregime scheme. They share the same globally stiffly accurate IMEX Runge-Kutta discretization and are synchronized at every internal stage through kinetic-to-fluid moment projections and fluid-to-kinetic lifting. This stage-wise coupling maintains temporal consistency across model interfaces, while the asymptotic-preserving structure ensures compatibility with the fluid limit as the Knudsen number becomes small. The active description is selected in each cell through moment-realizability indicators derived from successive Chapman-Enskog approximations. The hierarchy uses Euler in near-equilibrium regions, Navier-Stokes where first-order nonequilibrium corrections are sufficient, and the full Boltzmann equation where a kinetic description is required. Using Navier-Stokes as the intermediate level avoids evolving a velocity distribution in mildly nonequilibrium regions, which is particularly advantageous on unstructured meshes, where kinetic transport dominates the cost. The spatial discretization combines finite-volume WENO reconstruction on triangular meshes with a conservative fast spectral method for the Boltzmann collision operator. Numerical experiments show that the method closely reproduces the full Boltzmann reference while significantly reducing the computational cost. These results suggest that tightly coupled AP model hierarchies are a viable alternative to interface-based domain decomposition for deterministic kinetic simulations in complex geometries.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Caparello, Lorenzo Pareschi, Thomas Rey

item.title: High-order positivity-preserving well-balanced schemes: combining flux globalization with modified Patankar deferred correction methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.21857v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Positivity-preserving schemes for hyperbolic balance laws are typically built from the Zhang-Shu limiter and strong-stability-preserving Runge-Kutta (SSP-RK) time stepping, at the cost of a restrictive time-step condition. The modified Patankar deferred correction (mPDeC) method removes this restriction, offering high-order accuracy, conservation, and unconditional positivity. However, its solution-dependent Patankar weights make the time update nonlinear, so, unlike with RK methods, preserving (steady and moving) equilibria, i.e., well-balancing (WB), is no longer straightforward. In this paper, we construct high-order, WB, positivity-preserving mPDeC schemes by combining mPDeC with a flux-globalization approach. We demonstrate the idea on the one-dimensional shallow water equations, using a WB A-WENO spatial discretization, and introduce a modified local characteristic decomposition that remains stable in the presence of dry states. Numerical experiments on one-dimensional benchmarks confirm that the method satisfies the desired properties.
item.dc:creator: Philipp \"Offner, Michael Redle, Davide Torlo

item.title: A Hybridizable Discontinuous Galerkin Method for Time-Modulated Drude--Lorentz Media
item.description: arXiv:2610.21991v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate and analyze a hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) method for Maxwell's equations coupled to four time-modulated Drude--Lorentz models: modulated in-coupling, modulated polarization density, modulated current density, and modulated effective mass. The use of electric displacement and model-dependent continuous material states gives a common treatment of temporal interfaces while preserving the distinct physical transmission rules. We derive energy and stability estimates, establish spatial and event-aligned time-error bounds, and separate time-integration error from error caused by misplaced switching times. Numerical experiments in three dimensions and in reduced modal systems confirm the predicted spatial, temporal, and switch-timing behavior, including the field-jump effect specific to the polarization-density model.
item.dc:creator: Jeonghun J. Lee

item.title: Finite Volume Convergence for a Heat Equation with a Measure-Valued Source
item.description: arXiv:2610.22063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Past work with Tom Seidman analyzed the spatial convergence order of the numerical finite element method applied to time-dependent diffusion-reaction equations with a measure-valued source term. For smooth source terms, the numerical method has second-order accuracy, but the non-smooth source terms introduce a limitation of the order that depends on the spatial dimension. This work in honor of Tom extends the analysis to the finite volume method in its clas- sical two-point flux form and shows that the regularity of the source term reduces the convergence order to 1 in two and 0.5 in three spatial dimensions which is reduced from the nominal second-order and depends on the space dimension. Computational tests with a point source modeled by a Dirac delta distribution exhibit the behavior predicted by the analytical results.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Gobbert, Martin Kru\v{z}\'{\i}k, Andreas Meister, Michael Muscedere

item.title: The ReLU Matrix Decomposition: NP-Hardness, Ill-Posedness, and ReLU-Rank
item.description: arXiv:2610.22255v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ReLU Matrix Decomposition (RMD) approximates a sparse, nonnegative m-by-n matrix X by max(0, WH), where W is an m-by-r matrix, H is an r-by-n matrix, and r is the rank of the decomposition. The most common formulation, referred to as Fro-RMD, minimizes the Frobenius norm of X - max(0, WH) over W and H. We prove that Fro-RMD is NP-hard, even for binary matrices and r = 1; to the best of our knowledge, this is the first complexity result for RMD. We also show that Fro-RMD is ill-posed, in the sense that its infimum may not be attained. We then turn to exact RMD, that is, X = max(0, WH), and define the ReLU-rank of X as the smallest r for which such a decomposition exists. We interpret exact RMDs geometrically as configurations of points and hyperplanes in an r-dimensional space, associated with the rows of W and the columns of H, respectively. Building on this interpretation, we derive upper bounds on the ReLU-rank of diagonal, block-diagonal, and block-sparse matrices and, under an additional structural assumption, improve the best known bound for block-diagonal matrices. Finally, we propose two formulations of exact RMD as feasibility problems: a nonconvex quadratically constrained program, which can be tackled by global solvers such as Gurobi, and a formulation based on the latent model of Saul, (``A nonlinear matrix decomposition for mining the zeros of sparse data', SIMODS, 2022), which we tackle using alternating projections for which we establish local convergence together with asymptotic convergence rates. We compare these two approaches on some numerical examples.
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Seraghiti, Arnaud Vandaele, Nicolas Gillis

item.title: Real-Arithmetic Sketched Eigensolvers for Symmetric Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2610.22261v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we develop sketched variants of subspace iteration and TraceMIN, called sSI and sTraceMIN, for real symmetric eigenvalue problems by combining basis whitening with the sketched Rayleigh-Ritz (sRR) procedure. The nonsymmetric projected matrix in sRR may have nonreal eigenpairs, leading to complex arithmetic and additional computational costs. We overcome this difficulty using a real Schur formulation of sRR that keeps the iterations in real arithmetic. We further develop procedures for characteristic subspace selection and convergence monitoring within this formulation. On the theoretical side, we discuss suitable subspace embedding assumptions for sketched eigensolvers that use a fixed sketching matrix throughout the iterations. Under a mild embedding assumption, we establish local convergence results for sSI and sTraceMIN. Numerical experiments demonstrate runtime savings of up to 39% for sSI and 21% for sTraceMIN relative to their standard counterparts on the test problems.
item.dc:creator: Jingyu Liu, Yuqi Liu

item.title: An implicit multiscale solver for steady kinetic equations based on wave-particle decomposition
item.description: arXiv:2610.20660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Steady kinetic computations require accurate transport on meshes that do not resolve the mean free path and efficient removal of slowly decaying macroscopic errors. We develop a closed wave-particle decomposition (WPD) and a residual-based implicit solver for this problem. The wave accumulates only the Maxwellian along a local characteristic horizon and is determined by the conservative variables; the particle carries the kinetic complement and collision remainder. Under moment compatibility, the closed system is equivalent to the kinetic equation. For the Bhatnagar-Gross-Krook and Shakhov models, a hydrodynamic expansion gives the wave and particle contributions to the Euler and Navier-Stokes fluxes. The implicit iteration couples macroscopic prediction to microscopic correction through a discrete endpoint term and synchronizes the conservative moments after each accepted correction. Its stationary states satisfy the target discrete kinetic equation independently of the iteration controls. Formal analysis gives the smooth fixed-mesh fluid limit. Linear model analysis relates convergence to the horizon-to-relaxation ratio, incomplete macroscopic solves and explicit collision remainders. One- and two-dimensional computations of a normal shock, internal flows and hypersonic external flows test these properties across rarefied and continuum regimes. The results show kinetic fidelity and substantial reductions in iteration counts and wall time relative to the conventional iterative scheme near the continuum limit. Collision-model comparisons and parameter studies support the predicted convergence mechanisms.
item.dc:creator: Chang Liu, Kun Xu

item.title: Superfast Spectral Compressed Sensing with Quadratic Convergence
item.description: arXiv:2610.21068v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the spectral compressed sensing problem of recovering a spectrally sparse signal from linear compressive measurements. Exploiting the low-rank Hankel structure associated with the signal, we formulate a nonconvex fixed-rank optimization problem with a Hankel regularization. We propose a Superfast Iterative Hard Thresholding (SIHT) algorithm, where each iteration consists of a tangent-space least-squares update followed by a fixed-rank hard thresholding projection. SIHT is the first nonconvex algorithm with provable quadratic convergence for spectral compressed sensing. For random Gaussian measurements, it achieves exact recovery in the noiseless case and stable recovery in the noisy case with near-optimal sample complexity. To efficiently implement SIHT, we develop a parameterized conjugate gradient method for solving the least-squares subproblem, endowing SIHT with state-of-the-art computational and memory efficiency. Numerical experiments are provided to validate our results.
item.dc:creator: Xunmeng Wu, Jian-Feng Cai, Zongben Xu, Zai Yang

item.title: Stochastic Latent Twins: Learning Stochastic Solution Operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.21084v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scientific prediction under uncertainty requires more than a single future state: it requires the distribution of possible outcomes. We show that this distribution-valued evolution can be learned directly as a stochastic solution operator between arbitrary source and target times. We introduce Stochastic Latent Twins, which represent the physical state through a deterministic encoder-decoder while placing stochasticity entirely in a probability-valued latent evolution map. This separation makes the stochastic transition law independent of the state representation and enables direct probabilistic prediction without recursive time stepping. We establish an end-to-end Wasserstein approximation theory that separates representation and latent-transition errors, derive stability guarantees, and develop a distributional theory of physics conformity with latent-to-physical transfer bounds and conformity by construction. The resulting framework can be learned directly from observed transitions and supports forward prediction, backward conditional evolution, one-shot generation, and physics-conforming stochastic dynamics within the same formulation. Numerical experiments ranging from linear and non-Gaussian SDEs to stochastic Lorenz dynamics, generative modeling, a stochastic Hamiltonian system, and a two-dimensional stochastic Burgers equation verify the theory, expose the distinct roles of state representation and transition-family expressivity, compare favorably with recent stochastic and one-step generative methods, and demonstrate exact physical conservation by construction. More broadly, Stochastic Latent Twins provide a step toward scientific surrogates that represent not only the evolution of a system, but also its uncertainty and physical structure, opening new opportunities across uncertainty quantification, data assimilation, inverse problems, control, and digital twins.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Chung, Jack Michael Solomon, Deepanshu Verma

item.title: Reconstructing constant point heat sources from few temperature sensors: sparse selection and spatial resolution
item.description: arXiv:2610.21301v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Thermal diffusion and measurement noise can obscure the number and individual parameters of localized heat sources. We study the reconstruction of constant positive point sources from temperature histories at a few sensors, without prescribing the source count. Orthogonal matching pursuit or least angle regression selects candidate locations from a unit-response dictionary. These candidates initialize continuous constrained fits, and a noise-based discrepancy rule selects the smallest accepted model among the attempted fits. The response analysis distinguishes rejection of a merged one-source model from accurate recovery of the individual sources. It gives a projected quadratic residual for a close pair, a weak direction in the two-source parameters, and a conditional bound for recovering the total strength and strength-weighted center of an unresolved cluster. A local Gaussian approximation relates one-source rejection to noise and separation. Paired numerical tests compare sensor and time-sampling budgets, noise levels, and source separations. Finite-plate data generated independently of the inverse response and a three-dimensional example assess the same fitting procedure. In the tested configurations, source-count selection and individual parameter recovery differ substantially, while unresolved pairs can retain accurate aggregate estimates. The framework combines reconstruction with a local interpretation of which heat-source information the observations support.
item.dc:creator: Xiaomei Yang, Zhiliang Deng

item.title: Data-driven Smooth-to-hard Spectral Regularization for General Linear Inverse Problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.21664v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The logistic smooth-to-hard shrinker is the proximal map of an explicit saturating spectral penalty for general linear inverse problems. Its exact weak convexity yields a unique scaled update and proximal-gradient stationarity guarantees, while independent validation provides finite-grid parameter-selection control. We use MRI as an illustrative example.
item.dc:creator: Guanzhong Yang, Zi Wang, Guang Yang

item.title: Change the Number, Change the Answer: Assessing Rating Scale Sensitivity in LLM-Based Text Scoring
item.description: arXiv:2610.22187v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in computational social science to assign scalar scores to social and psychological constructs. However, studies use different rating scales, and whether their scores remain comparable across scale designs is understudied. To address this gap, we define and systematically investigate scale sensitivity, the variation in LLM-generated scores caused by rating scale design. We distinguish numerical sensitivity, changes in normalized scores, from semantic sensitivity, changes in score interpretation. To assess both, our experimental design crosses 2 formats (continuous vs. ordinal), 4 ranges (3, 5, 11, and 21 points), and 2 signs (signed vs. unsigned) across 3 tasks (political leaning, sentiment, and toxicity), 2 prompting strategies (zero-shot and rubric-based), and 5 LLMs. We find that changing one design element shifts normalized scores by about 0.10 on average and changes the category of roughly 20% of texts. Sensitivity is greatest for toxicity, the only unipolar construct examined. Also, rubric-based prompting does not reduce sensitivity compared with zero-shot prompting. We provide practical guidance for designing more reliable LLM-based text scoring and highlight the need for robustness checks across alternative scales.
item.dc:creator: Wonjeong Jo, Gyuwan Kim, Ming Shan Hee

item.title: Computational Models for Magnetic Drug Targeting, Part 1: Derivation and Numerical Simulation of a Thermodynamically Consistent Magneto Two-phase Flow Model
item.description: arXiv:2508.04360v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by Magnetic Drug Targeting (MDT), we derive a thermodynamically consistent two-phase model for the coupled dynamics of superparamagnetic iron oxide nanoparticles (SPIONs), a carrier fluid, and the magnetic field. The model includes a convection-diffusion equation for the SPION dispersion volume density and a modified Navier-Stokes system for the mixture velocity with SPION-dependent density and viscosity, an additional momentum flux due to relative SPION motion, and a magnetic body force. Additionally, the SPIONs interact with a quasi-static Maxwell system through their magnetization which is of Langevin type. The coupled system satisfies a global energy-dissipation balance. Moreover, we develop a semi-implicit finite element scheme with explicit flux-corrected transport stabilization and simulate the attraction of an initially localized SPION dispersion towards an external magnet in a system closed to mass exchange, using parameter values representative of MDT settings. The resulting SPION redistribution and induced flow are analyzed through physical observables, including energy and dissipation contributions and iron mass within a target region. Temporal convergence studies assess the ability of the numerical scheme to reproduce the energy-dissipation balance. Finally, we study the influence of individual coupling mechanisms on particle accumulation, maximum iron density, and peak flow velocity.
item.dc:creator: Eberhard B\"ansch, Jonas Knoch, Nicolas Neuss, Maria Neuss-Radu

item.title: On the choice of viscous discontinuous Galerkin discretization for entropy correction artificial viscosity methods
item.description: arXiv:2602.23210v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Entropy correction artificial viscosity (ECAV) is an approach for enforcing a semi-discrete entropy inequality through an entropy dissipative correction term. The resulting method can be implemented as an artificial viscosity with an extremely small viscosity coefficient. In this work, we analyze ECAV when the artificial viscosity is discretized using a local discontinuous Galerkin (LDG) method. We prove an $O(h)$ upper bound on the ECAV coefficient, indicating that ECAV does not result in a restrictive time-step condition. We additionally show that ECAV is contact preserving, and compare ECAV to traditional shock capturing artificial viscosity methods.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Q. Van Fleet, Jesse Chan

item.title: An immersed peridynamics method for fluid-driven damage and failure of anisotropic materials
item.description: arXiv:2603.16046v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The immersed peridynamics (IPD) method is a fluid-structure interaction (FSI) model to simulate fluid-driven material damage and failure of an immersed structure, in which a peridynamic (PD) constitutive correspondence model is employed within a classical immersed boundary (IB)-type framework to describe stresses, forces, and structural deformations of a structural body, instead of classical continuum mechanics. This paper introduces an extension of the IPD method to simulate fluid-driven structural deformation, damage, and failure of anisotropic materials with complex geometries. We use quadrature rules attached to finite element (FE) meshes to generate both the PD points and their associated weights, which are used to approximate the PD integrals. We demonstrate that non-uniform discretizations improve both accuracy and volume conservation of hyperelastic materials along with accurately represented boundaries. To capture realistic biomaterial behaviors, we incorporate hyperelastic constitutive models including both isotropy and anisotropy into the proposed IPD method. In addition, a ductile failure model is adopted to simulate progressive damage and failure in anisotropic materials. For non-failure cases, our numerical simulations demonstrate that the extended IPD method yields comparable accuracy with similar numbers of structural degrees of freedom for different choices of peridynamic horizon sizes. For failure tests, we investigate the effect of a fiber orientation on deformations and failure processes using realistic biomaterial models with varying fiber directions. We further demonstrate that the developed method generates grid-converged simulations of damage growth, crack formation and propagation, and rupture under large deformations, including purely fluid-driven failure processes.
item.dc:creator: Keon Ho Kim, Boyce E. Griffith

item.title: Accelerating an ensemble of variational data assimilations with randomized preconditioning
item.description: arXiv:2605.23571v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ensembles of variational data assimilations (EDA) require solving systems of linear equations with iterative methods. The solution process can be accelerated using a limited memory preconditioner constructed with approximations of the leading eigenpairs of the Hessian matrix. Randomized methods for low-rank matrix approximations provide a feasible approach for computing these eigenpairs. These methods use a random sketching matrix to obtain a low-rank representation of the Hessian matrix, which is then used for computing the eigendecomposition. The sketching matrix highly influences the quality of the approximation. In this paper, we show how the structure of the EDA can be exploited to construct a suitable sketching matrix, i.e., using the differences of the right-hand sides of the linear systems of equations. Idealised numerical experiments with the Lorenz-96 model show that the resulting preconditioner is able to accelerate the EDA solution process for all ensemble members, even if constructed from the control member only.
item.dc:creator: I. Dau\v{z}ickait\.e, S. G\"urol, M. Destouches, L. Berre, A. T. Weaver

item.title: Statistical comparison of reconstruction methods for the inverse boundary problem of the one-dimensional wave equation
item.description: arXiv:2605.28415v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Several numerical reconstruction algorithms for the inverse boundary value problem of the 1-dimensional wave equation exist. In this paper we revisit two of them, the Sondhi-Gopinath (SG) method from 1971 and the Korpela-Lassas-Oksanen (KLO) method from 2016. Our main contribution is a systematic and statistical comparison of the performance of these two well established methods. The stability of the SG algorithm, even in practical applications, is well known. KLO has a regularisation scheme with a theoretical proof, and is an evolution of the boundary control method. Both are based on the idea of constructing solutions that are characteristic functions of a set at a given time. This similarity has been pointed out before, but no systematic comparison has been published. We compare the performance of the two algorithms with noisy simulated data. The application in our mind is the reconstruction of the internal cross-sectional area of a pressurised fluid pipe. The area corresponds to the first order $\partial_x$-term of the wave equation. Instead of just observing the performance on a few test cases, we generate $n=1000$ random area profiles of various smoothness levels and measurement noise up to $10\%$ of the signal energy and perform statistical tests. SG and KLO have a difference of one time-derivative in their standard boundary data, which complicates the analysis. Our results show that SG performs better in the low noise regime, and KLO with high noise. SG is easier to implement and runs faster.
item.dc:creator: Samuel Agenorwoth, Emilia Bl{\aa}sten

item.title: LGNO: A Local-Global Neural Operator for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws
item.description: arXiv:2606.18221v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Solutions of hyperbolic conservation laws exhibit both smooth structures across large scales and sharp localized features such as shocks and contact discontinuities, making them difficult to approximate accurately with existing neural operators. The Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) captures long-range interactions well but tends to smear localized structures through excessive numerical dissipation. To address this, we propose a Local-Global Neural Operator (LGNO) that learns a one-step discrete flow map by combining a global FNO branch for representing smooth dynamics at large scales with a local multiresolution branch for enhancing localized discontinuities and nonsmooth features. The model is trained with a one-step loss that combines a physical space prediction term and a spectral penalty on high frequencies to suppress spurious oscillations near steep fronts. On a large collection of benchmarks in one and two dimensions, LGNO consistently outperforms FNO baselines with matched parameter counts, reducing one-step errors by factors of 2-5 and remaining significantly more accurate over long autoregressive rollouts. Most strikingly, although it is trained only on short-time data from a high-order WENO-Z scheme, the long-time rollout of LGNO on a coarse $256^2$ grid exhibits lower numerical dissipation than the same WENO-Z scheme run on a finer $512^2$ grid, while being orders of magnitude cheaper to evaluate. These results suggest that, with an appropriate architecture and training objective, learned operators can effectively learn discrete flow maps. They further suggest that such learned operators have the potential to control long-time numerical dissipation better than the conventional shock-capturing schemes that generate the training data.
item.dc:creator: Hao Wang, Chi-Wang Shu, Qi Tang

item.title: Optimal Polynomial Tractability Exponents for the Inverse Star Discrepancy
item.description: arXiv:2607.23571v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The inverse of the star discrepancy $n^\ast(d, \varepsilon)$ satisfies \[ d \varepsilon^{-1} \lesssim n^{\ast}(d,\varepsilon)\lesssim d\varepsilon^{-2} \] for all $d \in \mathbb{N}$ and $0 < \varepsilon < \varepsilon_0$. The upper bound was established by Heinrich, Novak, Wasilkowski and Wo\'{z}niakowski (2001), while the lower bound is due to Hinrichs (2004). Steinerberger (2023) subsequently gave an elementary proof of the latter result. These bounds imply that the inverse of the star discrepancy depends linearly on the dimension, but the exact exponent of $\varepsilon^{-1}$ had remained open. In this paper we prove a lower bound which shows that the exponent $2$ of $\varepsilon^{-1}$ in the upper bound cannot be improved. More precisely, for every $0<\alpha<1$ and fixed $0<A\le B$, there exist constants $c_{\alpha,B}>0$ and $\varepsilon_{\alpha,A}>0$ such that, for every $0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_{\alpha,A}$ and every integer $d$ satisfying \[ A\varepsilon^{-\alpha}\le d\le B\varepsilon^{-\alpha}, \] one has \[ n^\ast(d,\varepsilon) \ge c_{\alpha,B}\,d\,\varepsilon^{-(2-\alpha)}. \] Along these polynomial strips the right-hand side is of order $\varepsilon^{-2}$. Consequently, every uniform polynomial upper estimate $n^{\ast}(d,\varepsilon)\le C d^q\varepsilon^{-p}$ must satisfy $p\ge2$. Together with the lower bound of Hinrichs (2004), which forces $q\ge1$, this proves that the exponents $p=2$ and $q=1$ in the Heinrich--Novak--Wasilkowski--Wo\'{z}niakowski upper bound are individually optimal. In particular, the optimal exponent $p^\ast = 2$.
item.dc:creator: Josef Dick

item.title: Sharp bounds for non-adaptive randomized approximation of high-dimensional vectors
item.description: arXiv:2608.00148v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the complexity of approximating the finite-dimensional vector space embedding $\ell_p^m \hookrightarrow \ell_q^m$ for $2 \leq p < q \leq \infty$ based on non-adaptive randomized algorithms that use up to $n$ arbitrary linear functionals as information on a problem instance $x \in \mathbb{R}^m$, where $n \ll m$. We prove lower bounds on the non-adaptive randomized approximation error with a joint dependence on $(n,m)$ matching previously known upper bounds.
item.dc:creator: Robert J. Kunsch, Marcin Wnuk

item.title: A priori error estimator for reduced-order models based on the higher-order Craig-Bampton method in dynamic substructuring
item.description: arXiv:2608.05625v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The higher-order Craig-Bampton (HCB) method improves reduced-model accuracy through successive residual-mode enrichments. This study proposes an a priori estimator for the eigenvalue error remaining in the first-order HCB model (HCB-1) without using the full-order eigensolution. The estimator is defined as the relative difference between the HCB-1 and HCB-2 eigenvalues. Under symmetric Ritz approximation assumptions, ordered positive eigenvalues, nested augmented spaces, and preservation of retained eigenvalues by the System Equivalent Reduction Expansion Process (SEREP), the estimator is shown to be non-negative and to provide a lower bound on the relative HCB-1 eigenvalue error. A projection-based expression and an exact error identity are also derived, clarifying the conditions under which the estimator is accurate and showing that the lower-bound property alone does not guarantee a prescribed tolerance. Numerical results for a plate, an elbow pipe, and a reactor pressure vessel show estimation-to-error ratios of about 0.85-0.99, while a cost assessment reports the additional expense associated with the HCB-2 reference solution.
item.dc:creator: Jaemin Kim, Seung-Hwan Boo

item.title: The Normal Procrustes Problem: A Riemannian Optimization Approach
item.description: arXiv:2608.19513v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For given $m \times n$ data matrices $X, Y$, we investigate the Normal Procrustes Problem---the least squares optimization problem that aims to minimize $\|AX-Y\|_F^2$, where $A$ is constrained to be a normal $m \times m$ matrix. As far as the author of this article is aware, no other method that attempts to solve the Normal Procrustes Problem exists in the literature; we thus propose what is, to our knowledge, the first such method. We, furthermore, adapt our approach to address the Real Normal Procrustes Problem, where $A$ must be real. In our treatment of these problems, we first reduce our complex and real objective functions to be purely optimizable over the Riemannian manifolds of the unitary and real orthogonal matrices, respectively. This reduction enables us to apply techniques in Riemannian manifold optimization to approximate solutions to both. The Closest Normal Matrix and Real Closest Normal Matrix Problems are both special cases of their respective Procrustes Problems (by setting $m = n$ and $X = I_m$) and have been previously studied in the literature. Our approach thus recovers a novel Riemannian optimization method for approximating solutions to both these problems. We further numerically test the performance of our method across all such problems (including against previously developed algorithms on the Closest Normal Matrix Problems) and obtain competitive residuals and favorable scaling in wall-clock time.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Bierly

item.title: Almost $L^\infty$-stability of the Ritz projection for the integral fractional Laplacian with $0<s\leq \tfrac12$
item.description: arXiv:2610.11795v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $0<s\leq 1/2$ and $d\geq 1$, the $\widetilde H^s$-projection onto piecewise linear finite element spaces on quasi-uniform meshes of a bounded Lipschitz domain in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with a uniform exterior ball condition is almost stable in the maximum norm. The mesh domain need not coincide with the original domain.
item.dc:creator: Jia Li, Shuonan Wu

item.title: Convergence of Least Squares Methods for PDEs on R^d with Shallow ReLU^k Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.14457v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish inverse inequalities in Gaussian Sobolev norms for shallow $\mathrm{ReLU}^k$ trial spaces. The estimates identify the sharp regularity threshold and quantify the dependence on parameter separation and bias magnitude. Based on these estimates, we prove convergence of weighted least squares discretizations of linear PDEs on $\mathbb R^d$ using shallow networks with prescribed inner parameters and finitely many residual samples in an expanding ball. Under suitable stability and regularity assumptions, we obtain an error bound of order $h^{k+(d+1)/2-r}\delta_\pm^{-(S-r)}$ in the Gaussian Sobolev norm of order $S$, up to logarithmic factors, where $r$ is the PDE order, $h$ is the parameter fill distance, and $\delta_\pm$ is the antipodal separation. The convergence results cover deterministic and random sampling and extend to fixed bounded regions by restriction. We construct parameter sets with $\delta_\pm\asymp h$, yielding a convergence rate in terms of the network width that matches a lower bound up to logarithmic factors. Numerical experiments support the theoretical results and provide practical guidance on balancing accuracy and stability.
item.dc:creator: Tong Mao, Lei Shi, Hanfei Zhou

item.title: SUPN: Shallow Universal Polynomial Networks for Efficient Function Approximation
item.description: arXiv:2511.21414v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep neural networks (DNNs) and Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs) are flexible function approximators, but their accuracy can require substantial network depth, width, and trainable parameter counts. Beyond making the resulting networks less transparent, large parameter spaces can increase training cost and produce solutions that are sensitive to optimization and parameter initialization, leading to variability in generalization error. For these reasons, we propose Shallow Universal Polynomial Networks (SUPNs), which retain a single hidden layer while increasing the expressivity of each unit through a learnable multivariate polynomial inside each activation, which we refer to as a polynomial pre-activation. This construction trades architectural depth and width for greater expressivity within each hidden unit, reducing parameter counts and training cost while preserving a shallow computational graph. We establish two complementary universal approximation results: SUPNs are universal by increasing network width at fixed polynomial complexity, as in classical shallow-network approximation, and by increasing polynomial complexity at fixed finite width. We further prove that finite SUPNs can approach the best approximation attainable in a prescribed polynomial space to arbitrary relative tolerance, derive explicit quasi-optimal parameters, and establish corresponding convergence rates. We empirically evaluate SUPNs against DNNs, KANs, and polynomial projection on smooth, nonsmooth, and discontinuous function-approximation problems in one, two, and ten dimensions using more than 16,000 trained models. Across the target functions studied, SUPNs frequently achieve lower approximation error and variability than DNNs and KANs at comparable parameter counts while retaining lower training cost, supporting their use as efficient function approximators when the target structure is not known a priori.
item.dc:creator: Zachary Morrow, Michael Penwarden, Brian Chen, Aurya Javeed, Akil Narayan, John D. Jakeman

item.title: A Homotopy Framework for Constrained Multiobjective Optimization
item.description: arXiv:2605.00003v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a homotopy continuation framework for computing Karush--Kuhn--Tucker (KKT) points of constrained multiobjective optimization problems. The proposed homotopy map continuously deforms an easily solvable system into the KKT system associated with the original multiobjective problem, yielding a deterministic continuation path. Under the stated regularity and reference-point cone avoidance assumptions, we establish the existence of a smooth, bounded continuation path whose set of accumulation points as the homotopy parameter approaches zero is nonempty and consists of KKT points. The framework is implemented using two numerical continuation algorithms including an enhanced pseudo-arclength predictor--corrector strategy with adaptive step-size control and branch-restarting mechanisms to improve robustness for challenging nonconvex and degenerate problems. Numerical experiments demonstrate that the proposed method remains effective even when initialized from nonfeasible points, indicating practical robustness beyond the theoretical guarantees. Comparative studies evaluate the proposed framework against classical scalarization approaches and the evolutionary algorithms. Experiments on benchmark problems, disconnected and nonconvex multiobjective problems, analytically solvable three-objective problems, and a multiobjective IEEE 5-bus optimal power flow problem demonstrate the ability of the framework to compute KKT points in a variety of constrained settings. The results also highlight the effects of initialization and the limitations of continuation-based methods in recovering complete Pareto-front coverage. Overall, the proposed framework provides a deterministic and interpretable approach to computing Pareto-critical (KKT) points in constrained multiobjective optimization.
item.dc:creator: Olaoluwa Ogunleye, Guangming Yao, Jianhua Zhang, Manh Bui

item.title: Smooth Hard-Thresholding for Singular Values with Stein's Unbiased Risk Estimate
item.description: arXiv:2606.06632v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Low-rank matrix denoising is a central primitive in patch-based image restoration and many other inverse problems. Classical SVD-based image denoising methods often choose a truncation rank by matching residual singular-value energy with an estimated noise energy, but this rule is not a finite-sample risk principle because a fitted low-rank approximation inevitably absorbs part of the noise. This paper develops a mathematically rigorous alternative based on Stein's unbiased risk estimate (SURE). Since singular value hard thresholding is discontinuous and does not satisfy the hypotheses of Stein's lemma, we introduce a logistic smooth hard-threshold spectral estimator. We prove that the smooth shrinker satisfies the regularity conditions required by a spectral-estimator version of Stein's lemma, and therefore admits an exactly unbiased fixed-threshold risk estimate under Gaussian noise. For a fixed observed matrix and a finite set of candidate thresholds separated from the observed singular values, the ordering of the fixed-threshold smooth SURE objective eventually agrees with a simple limiting score. The limiting score has the same algebraic form as the biased hard-threshold SURE formula, but here it is used only as a computational device for ranking finite candidates. Selecting the minimizing threshold is a data-adaptive tuning step; the selected SURE value should not be interpreted as an unbiased risk estimate of the finally selected estimator.
item.dc:creator: Guanzhong Yang, Zi Wang, Guang Yang

item.title: Feature-preserving Latent-EnKF for Data Assimilation of Flows with Shocks
item.description: arXiv:2606.12559v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF) is widely adopted for sequential data assimilation, but fails for solutions with discontinuities, such as shocks in compressible flows. For ensembles with uncertainty in discontinuity location, the EnKF analysis can lose physical consistency, which can be viewed through three lenses: (i) bimodal pointwise statistics in the forecast ensemble, (ii) mixed-sign analysis weights in the affine superposition of forecast members, and (iii) spatially distributed Kalman-gain profiles that modify the state around a discontinuity rather than translating it coherently. In order to preserve flow features in the analysis state and, as such, maintain physical consistency, a feature-preserving latent-EnKF is introduced. The proposed method performs the ensemble update in a low-dimensional latent space learned by a coordinate-conditioned auto-decoder. The latent representation retains near-Gaussian ensemble statistics and provides coordinates in which flow features vary coherently across the forecast ensemble. The EnKF updates performed on the latent codes are decoded into coherent changes in the represented flow features, translating shocks through coordinate morphing rather than superposing them at displaced locations. The corresponding Kalman-gain profiles generated by the latent-EnKF exhibit an approximately step-like variation across the discontinuities, allowing the fronts to translate while preserving sharp features and monotonicity. Sod shock-tube, Mach~2 shock-cylinder, and immersed-body shape-inference tests with sparse, noisy observations demonstrate accurate recovery of shocks and contact discontinuities without spurious oscillations.
item.dc:creator: Hemanth Chandravamsi, Hangchuan Hu, Ponkrshnan Thiagarajan, Tamer A. Zaki

item.title: Blockwise Stabilized Adaptive Cubic Regularization with Subsolvers via Recurrence
item.description: arXiv:2608.22129v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Overparameterized networks often have ill-conditioned, saddle rich loss landscapes. They are usually trained with first-order methods that struggle on those landscapes, while many second-order methods stay infeasible at scale. Some scalable cubic methods replace the Hessian by a computationally cheap approximation and drop the exact block curvature. This paper introduces ARC-block, a blockwise adaptive regularization with cubics (ARC) optimizer. For each parameter tensor it minimizes a cubic model over the true block Hessian, with a per-block adaptive cubic constant and a monotone guard on the full loss. Large tensors are handled matrix-free in a Lanczos-built Krylov subspace. ARC-block's CubicKrylov subsolver's descent is monotone with a per-block cubic decrease bound. For exact steps, and for Krylov steps that meet the Cartis--Gould--Toint residual test, we provide an $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{B}\varepsilon^{-3/2})$ sweep bound above a cross-block coupling floor. Another subsolver, ARC-$\varphi_1$, uses a trust-controlled exponential relaxation step. Among the cubic Newton methods evaluated here, these are the only ones whose steps stay exact on every parameter block (within the Krylov subspace), including on a $91.4$M-parameter implicit neural representation (INR). Run to convergence on FINER 2D image-fitting INR network, ARC-$\varphi_1$ reaches $133.5$ dB peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR), with no post peak collapse. Tuned Adam peaks at $78.2$ dB at $2{,}629$ s (step ${\sim}625$k, about $44$ minutes), further steps degrade its PSNR. On the same benchmark, SOAP, L-BFGS, and the scalable diagonal cubic method AdaCubic stay at or below Adam's $78.2$ dB peak. Over the benchmark's 20 images, run to a plateau rule, ARC-$\varphi_1$'s per-image PSNR has median $132.4$ and mean $131.5\pm3.3$ dB against tuned Adam's $72.8\pm4.5$ dB.
item.dc:creator: Rodion Podorozhny
